title: Protestants: every sin by nature merits eternal death and God’s wrath
source_text: I. Theologi Protestantes ante omnia uno consensu constituunt peccatum omne natura sua, mortem aeternam, & Dei odium atque iram mereri; nec ullum esse peccatum, quantumlibet leve hominum judicio videri queat, quod non possit a Deo poena sempiterna puniri, & hominem Dei amore excludere, si Deus cum homine rigide agere velit. Juxta illud legis Mosaicae, Maledictus omnis qui non permanserit in omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro legis hujus.
pass_a_gloss: Protestant theologians before all else with one consent establish that every sin by its nature merits eternal death and the hatred and wrath of God; nor is there any sin, however light it may seem in human judgment, that cannot be punished by God with everlasting penalty and exclude a man from God’s love, if God should wish to deal rigidly with man. According to that of the Mosaic law, Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all things that are written in the book of this law.
pass_b_english: Reformed consent opens Posterior: every sin, even the lightest in our eyes, deserves everlasting death if God deals by strict right.
The Mosaic curse on imperfect law-keeping sets the frame before any talk of lighter and heavier faults.

choices.why: Protestant claim that desert is intrinsic, not merely from event.
